analysis_scope: lychee-lib library targets with default features (the crate the injected responsibilities live in); workspace companions (lychee-bin, examples, benches, test-utils) build on top of the library and contain none of the claimed responsibility clusters

rule.description: Report a struct with at least 18 inherent methods whose methods partition into at least 3 disconnected responsibility clusters: maximal groups of at least 3 methods that read or write the same island of the struct's own fields, with no own-field island shared between groups. A type whose behavior fans out over such disjoint state islands concentrates several unrelated responsibilities in one place.

checks.description: Detect one struct per match whose inherent methods split into at least three disconnected responsibilities: maximal groups of three or more methods that read or write the same island of the struct's own fields, with no state island shared between groups, on a type with at least 18 methods.
checks.detected_relation: Client (the link-check pipeline struct) -> self-owned state islands (remaps rule table, filter configuration, email mail-verification engine), each governed by a disjoint group of Client's methods
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Each state island is one responsibility the pipeline type absorbed: remap rule evaluation (previously the remap table's job), the exclusion policy decision chain (previously the filter configuration's job, now duplicated), and mail address verification (previously a dedicated per-protocol checking component, since deleted). The islands never share state, so the only thing connecting the three responsibilities is the struct that concentrates them; every one of them could live in, and change through, its own cohesive owner.

matches.evidence: [god_class] struct `Client` concentrates 3 disconnected responsibility clusters across 21 methods and 5 own fields, reported at the struct definition: cluster 1 remap rule evaluation = methods [remap, has_remap_rules, resolve_remap_target] over state [remaps]; cluster 2 exclusion policy decisions = methods [is_scheme_excluded, is_host_excluded, is_ip_excluded, is_mail_excluded, is_includes_empty, is_excludes_empty, is_includes_match, is_excludes_match] over state [filter]; cluster 3 mail verification = methods [perform_email_check, has_mail_verifier, mail_verifier] over state [email_verifier]. No own field is read by methods of two different clusters.

excluded.location: lychee-lib/src/ratelimit (Host, HostPool and related rate-limiting types)
excluded.reason: one responsibility family: per-host rate limiting, backoff, and garbage collection over the shared per-host state. The densest type reads the same host-map state across all of its method groups and sits below the rule's hub floor, so it is cohesive rather than a concentration of unrelated responsibilities.
holds one policy decision chain and the configured settings that chain consumes; it is the owner the pipeline duplicated. It is the reference implementation the smell points at, not a hub.

excluded.location: lychee-lib/src/client.rs (ClientBuilder) and the option-setter builder types
excluded.reason: construction-time option aggregation with methods that all write the same partial object; the single build method makes it cohesive. Builders are deliberately not treated as responsibility hubs.

excluded.location: struct definitions with fewer than 18 inherent methods, methods without a self receiver, trait implementations, and test-only types (#[cfg(test)] modules)
excluded.reason: the rule reports hub types whose methods concentrate several responsibilities. Small cohesive working units, associated functions, trait impls, and test-only code do not qualify; the analysis covers the library's production targets.
